narratives.headline: Four games, all unders: Fox Under 6.5 assists leads a thin card while Portland's two questionable tags hang over two props
narratives.briefing: It is a light night with 4 games, and every prop on the card is an under, with no pick rated above Consider. The best of it is De'Aaron Fox Under 6.5 assists at conviction 47 and Tyler Herro Under 3.5 rebounds at conviction 46; the other three are rated Pass and Mikal Bridges has already moved past his play-to at −152. The record is mixed and should be read that way: morning picks are 3-2-0 (+0.54u), final picks 2-3-0 (-1.57u), and game lines are 13-26 (-14.41u) since 2026-11-11, so the totals below are leans only. Closing lines have moved toward the morning picks 3 times and against them 2 times. This edition goes out before official injury reports are final: we are waiting on Deni Avdija and Toumani Camara for Portland, which the model will re-price on the next run, and on Jonathan Kuminga for Minnesota; a morning search turned up no new news on any player in the props.

The risk is that you are betting against DraftKings, whose price says 44%, and Portland's frontcourt status (Avdija and Camara are both questionable) could change the picture once the model re-prices.

The case against is real: without Dylan Harper he has gone under in only 1 of 3, LAC is soft on point guard assists, and the market price says 44%, so this stays a Pass.

But the price of −152 is already past the play-to of −147, he has gone under in only 1 of 4 against MIN, and with Anthony Edwards out his minutes could run long, which is when this has missed.

narratives.briefing: Since the morning edition the prop card has turned over: Rudy Gobert Under 9.5 rebounds (+106) and Julian Champagnie Under 6.5 reb+ast were added, while Stephon Castle and Mikal Bridges were removed at 13:30Z and Brandin Podziemski was added and then removed at 18:46Z, all for no longer being +EV at tonight's lines. The market has leaned against the remaining unders on price: De'Aaron Fox has moved from −139 to −156 and Scoot Henderson from −130 to −139, both now past their play-to numbers. On the injury side, Kyle Kuzma and Myles Turner were ruled out and Ryan Rollins was upgraded from out to day-to-day, which lifted Tyler Herro Under 3.5 rebounds back to Consider at 47; Zach Edey was also ruled out for Memphis. On game lines, the POR @ MIL Under was removed (confidence fell 41 → 30), MIL +10.5 and GS @ MEM Over 225.5 were added, and NY -1.5 is back on the board, but game lines are 13-26 (-14.41u) since 2026-11-11, so treat all of them as leans only. The report itself is 6-4-0 (+1.50u) on morning picks with closing-line moves 8 toward and 2 against; still to come are final calls on Deni Avdija, Toumani Camara (both questionable for POR) and Jonathan Kuminga (questionable for MIN).

You are wrong if his 10.3 reb+ast/g history against LAC repeats or a blowout changes his minutes, and the price has slipped from +110 to +106.
cards.p|4395725|reb|Under: Herro projects at 3 rebounds against 3.5 with a 60% sim under, and POR is #3 toughest on shooting-guard rebounds. With Kuzma and Turner now ruled out his minutes are up 1.7, which is the main risk, and a change in Avdija, Camara or Rollins will re-price it on the next run.
cards.p|4683678|reb|Under: Henderson averages 1.6 rebounds over his last 10, went under 2.5 in 9 of those 10, and has gone under his posted line in 6 of 6 tracked games. The thin margin is the worry: 6 of his last 10 finished within 1 of this number, and at −139 the price is past the play-to line, so do not add here.
cards.p|3032976|reb|Under: New at 18:46Z: Gobert projects at 7.7 rebounds against 9.5 with 24.2 projected minutes, and NY games have 8% fewer rebounds available than the league. The case against is real: only 3 of his last 10 went under 9.5, and he goes over when he plays long, so a Kuminga absence that pushes his minutes up is what would make this wrong. Conviction is 44 (Pass).
cards.p|4066259|ast|Under: Fox averages 4.6 assists over his last 10 against a 6.5 line and stayed under even 5.5 in 6 of those 10. The price has run from −139 to −156, now past the play-to line, and LAC gives point guards 8% more assists than their norm; conviction has slipped to 43 (Pass).

narratives.headline: Final: Herro Under 4.5 still inside its play-to; Avdija, Camara and Kuminga still questionable close to tip
narratives.briefing: A light four-game Thursday where every prop on the board is an Under and none rates better than Consider at conviction 47. Tyler Herro Under 4.5 rebounds is the cleanest hold at −156, inside its play-to of −164. Scoot Henderson, Julian Champagnie and De'Aaron Fox have all drifted from their published prices but still sit inside tonight's play-to numbers, so they are holds, not adds. The market has mostly agreed with the morning picks (8 toward, 2 against), and the report is 6-4-0 in both editions, though the final has made less (+0.82u) than the morning (+1.50u). Three picks came off today: Stephon Castle and Mikal Bridges this morning, and Brandin Podziemski at 18:46 UTC once −149 removed the value. Still open at writing: Deni Avdija (foot) and Toumani Camara (abdomen) are questionable for Portland, and Jonathan Kuminga (right shoulder) is questionable for Minnesota, with a decision expected closer to tip.

The line jumped from 3.5 to 4.5 this afternoon, which costs price but adds a full rebound of room, and it stays playable down to −164. What makes it wrong: more than his projected 28.4 minutes with Turner out, or Avdija and Camara both sitting and reshaping Portland's rotation.

The risk is a thin margin (6 of his last 10 finished within 1 of the number) and a bigger role if Avdija or Camara sits, with Morant already out.

What makes it wrong: a blowout, where he has gone under only 15 of 34, or a repeat of his 10.3 reb+ast average against LAC.

The price has climbed from −139 to −156 and conviction is 43 (Pass), so this is a hold, not an add, with the play-to at −160. The worry is LAC giving point guards +8% assists and Dylan Harper being out, which leaves more of the ball in his hands.

It misses when he plays long (30.5 minutes in his overs vs 24.2 projected tonight), and Kuminga is still not cleared; the model re-prices if he sits.
